title: Events
objective: Listen to click and typing events with addEventListener, and use e.target and event delegation
story: On Planet DOM everything is waiting to react to you. A button being pressed, a letter being typed into a box: these are all **events**. Today you turn your page into a living control panel that listens to events.

sections.title: addEventListener: listen for an event
The event object and e.target
The input event and state
Removing a listener and event delegation

examples.note: Open the page and click the button a few times.

examples.title: Live preview and colors
examples.note: Type into the box, then click the color buttons. One listener handles all the color buttons.

tasks.title: Speed control
tasks.prompt:
Manage the `speed` state with buttons:

- When `#boost` (Speed up) is clicked, `speed` goes up by 10.
- When `#brake` (Slow down) is clicked, it goes down by 10, but **never below 0**.
- After every click, `#speed` shows the new speed.

Control Panel

Ready.

Speed: 0
hints: To stay at 0 or above: if (speed > 0) speed -= 10;

tasks.title: One-time launch
tasks.prompt:
The launch can only happen **once**. Complete the `onLaunch` function:

- `launches` goes up by 1 and `#info` shows `Launch! Engines running.`
- Then it removes itself with `removeEventListener`; a second click does nothing.

challenge.title: One listener
challenge.prompt:
Use **event delegation** for the route menu (`#menu`): add **one** `click` listener to `#menu`, not to the buttons.

- If a button was clicked, write `Route: Mars` into `#info` (from the button's text).
- Add the `selected` class to the clicked button and remove it from the other buttons in the menu.
- If something other than a button was clicked, do nothing.

Try adding a new button to the menu later and clicking it too!

project_task.title: Start button
project_task.prompt:
Now the start button (`#start-btn`) should work. When it's clicked:

- add the `hidden` class to `#start-screen` (the start screen disappears),
- remove the `hidden` class from `#game-panel` (the game panel shows),
- write `Score: 0 | Pilot: Ada` into `#hud` (the pilot's name comes from `game.pilot`).
